title: A sound heart
hookLine: the Day when wealth and sons won't help, only one who comes with a sound heart (26:88–89)
last: HE FEEDS ME; HE HEALS ME.

cards: Airports have a rule about what you can carry on. A small bag, a weight limit, and a whole list of things that have to be left behind at the gate. People stand at the security tray deciding, fast, what matters.
Ibrahim's prayer in Ash-Shu'ara keeps going after yesterday's verses, and it ends at a kind of gate. A day when almost everything people spend their lives collecting has to be left on the other side.
There's only one thing he says gets through.

teach.b: Ibrahim asks for wisdom, for good company, for an honest name among those who come later, for forgiveness for his father. Then he asks not to be disgraced on the day people are raised, and describes that day.
Pickthall: "The day when wealth and sons avail not (any man) Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart." Pickthall says a whole heart. The Arabic is qalb salim.
Qalb is heart. Salim means sound, safe, intact, unbroken. So what makes a heart salim?
Commentators gave several answers, and they stack. Free of associating anything with God. Free of doubt.
And some added: free of malice, envy and grudges toward other people. The Qur'an uses the same phrase once more, in As-Saffat, of Ibrahim himself: he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
So the one who names the sound heart is the one the Qur'an elsewhere says had it. There's a hadith in both Bukhari and Muslim that sits right beside this verse.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that in the body there is a lump of flesh; when it is sound, the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt, and it is the heart.
Elsewhere the Qur'an calls wealth and children an adornment of this life.

teach.h: FREE OF SHIRK, DOUBT AND GRUDGE.
teach.b: They just don't come through the gate. What comes through is a heart, and whether it arrives in one piece.

how: Many Muslims recite Ibrahim's prayer from Ash-Shu'ara and ask God for a sound heart, and some make a habit of forgiving others before sleeping.

o: a calm heart that feels no grief at all
a heart that has never once done wrong
a sound heart, whole and free of grudge

games.q: a sound heart — tap the pairs.
p: says Ibrahim came with a sound heart

s: the verse says wealth and children are bad
it says they don't avail on that Day; elsewhere the Qur'an calls them an adornment of this life.
qalb salim appears only once in the Qur'an
it appears again in As-Saffat, of Ibrahim himself.
the hadith of the lump of flesh says it is the heart
when it is sound, the whole body is sound.

games.q: you're standing at the gate on the Day Ibrahim describes. you can bring one thing through. what is it?
games.why: 26:88–89: wealth and sons avail not, save him who brings to God a whole, sound heart.

practice: Let a face come to mind, someone you're still a little sore with; not the worst wound you have, but a small one you could actually set down.

Notice where you carry it, in your jaw, your shoulders, your stomach, and loosen your grip on it for this minute, without excusing what happened. If you pray, you can ask for a sound heart, and for good for that person.

wordCard.voice: Qalb salim. A sound heart, whole and safe, free of shirk, doubt and grudge: the one thing Ibrahim says avails on the Day. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: qalb salim, a sound heart; Pickthall renders it a whole heart.

carryVoice: Your line: bring a sound heart. Everything else gets left behind at the tray. Until tomorrow.
